chapter_title: Concerning the Four Things over which People kill each other.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by later homiletic/application material (ethical description of worldly obsessions + exhortation to accept “faith” and the “physician”). It lacks the hallmark substrate feature of systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping (degree-structures, realm-to-realm correlations, etc.). The only clearly identifiable distinct layer is the hagiographic dialogue frame in ¶1; the remainder reads as moral/pastoral instruction rather than the oldest cosmological teaching substrate.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic editorial opening: “Once again he speaks to his disciples …” is a classic Kephalaia hagiographic frame marker.
Ethical/anthropological teaching about bodily appetite (“swelling of their body”), not a systematic cosmological-correspondential exposition; no cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Continues the fourfold moral catalogue (sexual intercourse/fornication). Descriptive vice-list register rather than substrate cosmology.
Wealth/boasting theme; again a moral critique of worldly attachment, not an internal cosmic mapping sequence.
War/tyranny/name in the world: social-ethical register (“received a name in the world”), consistent with later exhortative compilation material rather than the impersonal substrate voice.

Generalizing application (“All people… they struggle…”) and present-world anchoring (“on every tongue in the world”) signal editorial application voice rather than substrate description of cosmic mechanics.

Direct audience address (“I say to you”), exhortation to accept faith, and self-referential mediator language (“physician whom I have brought”) mark an applied homiletic layer. Although it uses Manichaean dualist terms (“separates the light from the darkness”), it is deployed as exhortation, not as systematic cosmos→cosmos teaching.
Moral conclusion about impermanence and death; eschatological warning style without correspondential system-building.
